articles.title: China’s Shenzhou 24 spacecraft docks at space station with first foreign astronaut
articles.summary: China on Wednesday launched the Shenzhou 24 spacecraft with three astronauts — two Chinese and a Pakistani — sending the first foreign crew member to its space station.
articles.body: China on Wednesday launched the Shenzhou 24 spacecraft with three astronauts — two Chinese and a Pakistani — sending the first foreign crew member to its space station. Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, 40, flew alongside Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo, 51, and Wu Yi, 39, after the craft blasted off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwestern China on Wednesday morning. It successfully separated from a rocket and entered its predetermined orbit. They later entered the space station and took group photos with three other astronauts from the Shenzhou 23 mission. The launch marked the first joint flight involving Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of China’s crewed space program. Hours earlier, crowds of people attended a send-off ceremony, with many holding up their phones to capture the moment. In Pakistan, shouts of “God is great!” and “Long live Pakistan-China friendship!” rang out as the spacecraft carrying Ali climbed toward space. Many families living thousands of miles from the launch site shared the milestone for their country’s space program through television broadcasts. In restaurants, customers followed the images on television, joining the celebrations with cries celebrating Pakistan’s friendship with China. Scientists at the headquarters of Pakistan’s space agency also watched the launch. Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari and Chinese President Xi Jinping exchanged letters congratulating each other, hailing the Pakistani astronaut’s inclusion in China’s space mission as a milestone in bilateral ties, according to a statement from Zardari’s office. Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported that Xi described China’s space station as a “boat” for peace, friendship and cooperation, and that China is willing to uphold the peaceful use of outer space with other countries and deepen cooperation. Pakistan’s Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif congratulated the nation on the launch, describing Ali’s mission as a source of national pride and an inspiration for Pakistani youth. “This is not just one astronaut’s journey, but the journey of 240 million Pakistanis,” he wrote on X. Sharif thanked China for including the Pakistani astronaut in the mission, saying the flight reflected close ties between the two countries and extended their cooperation into space. Pakistan’s Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives, Ahsan Iqbal, told reporters at the center that he hoped this would be the beginning of greater cooperation in the future. He also thanked Xi, the Chinese leadership, scientists and engineers. When asked if Pakistan could send astronauts independently, he said: “Certainly that day will come.” Iqbal said Ali carried not merely his name but the Pakistani flag on his shoulders and uniform, lifting the hopes, prayers and technological aspirations of Pakistanis into orbit. “The sky is no longer our limit, it is our launching pad,” he said in a statement, describing the mission as an inspiration for young Pakistanis hoping to pursue careers in science and technology. The joint flight is part of an agreement signed by China and Pakistan in February 2025. The crew will conduct more than 90 scientific experiments and technology tests during their mission, China’s official Xinhua News Agency reported earlier. Ali will conduct a photosynthetic cyanobacteria experiment in orbit during his short-term mission before returning to Earth aboard the Shenzhou 23 spacecraft, it said. While this was the first spaceflight for Ali and Wu, Tang has flown on two previous missions and has become the first astronaut to board the Tiangong space station three times, national broadcaster CCTV said. At a news conference on Tuesday, Tang said that differences in language, culture and psychology had made learning to work together more challenging on this mission, but that both sides’ efforts were paying off. In front of reporters, those efforts were reflected in Ali’s Mandarin proficiency. He cited a line of Chinese poetry about climbing one story higher to see farther. “It’s like my daily training. Day after day, reaching new heights,” he said in Mandarin. Speaking in English, he said he hoped the next chapter of space cooperation between the two countries would go from one astronaut in one flight to multiple joint flights and to the Moon, Mars and beyond. China is preparing for its first crewed lunar landing by 2030. The United States is widely seen as China’s main space rival, with NASA aiming to land astronauts on the lunar surface in 2028.

articles.title: 2 Libyan naval officers die of wounds from Ukrainian drone attack on Russian warship in Benghazi
articles.summary: Two Libyan naval officers died from wounds sustained in a weekend Ukrainian drone attack on a Russian warship moored in eastern Libya, Libyan authorities said.
articles.body: Two Libyan naval officers died from wounds sustained in a weekend Ukrainian drone attack on a Russian warship moored in eastern Libya, Libyan authorities said. The two men were pronounced dead Tuesday evening. They were wounded in the Sunday drone attack at the Benghazi Naval Base, the self-styled Libyan National Army, or LNA, said in a statement late Tuesday. The LNA’s General Command vowed to retaliate “at the appropriate time and place, and by the appropriate means.” Commanded by strongman Gen. Khalifa Hifter, the LNA is the most powerful group in Libya, a country fractured by years of civil war and chaos. It controls the country’s eastern and southern parts and has close relations with Russia. Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said forces deployed seven drones in the operation that struck the Russian navy corvette on Sunday. Libyan authorities said the ship had docked at the base to refuel and resupply. An initial investigation found that several Ukrainian sea drones were launched against the ship from a base operated by Ukrainian forces in western Libya, according to the two officials, who were briefed on the investigation. At least four drones were intercepted and destroyed, while two struck the corvette, a smaller warship designed to patrol coastal waters and escort other vessels, the officials said. One of them said at least 10 people, including Libyan and Russian nationals, were wounded. The officials, who are affiliated with the self-styled Libyan National Army, spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak to reporters. The strike has brought the Russia-Ukraine war to a new battleground, thousands of miles from Europe. It exposed how Moscow and Kyiv are using the fractured north African country as a theater for their wider confrontation. Oil-rich Libya, a strategically useful Mediterranean coastline and borders six nations, has had a fractured political landscape for over a decade. Its two administrations are backed by rival foreign powers. The internationally recognized government in Tripoli has cultivated ties with Ukraine and its Western allies, partly to support its efforts to stay in power, and to deter the flow of people hoping to reach Europe as migrants. It is backed by an array of loosely allied armed groups and militias. In eastern Libya, there is the government of Prime Minister Ossama Hammad, whose powerful ally is Hifter.

articles.title: Colombian security forces rescue hostages in supermarket siege
articles.summary: Colombian security forces freed all remaining hostages taken by armed men at a supermarket in the early hours of Wednesday, the police and government said, ending a day-long siege.
articles.body: Colombian security forces freed all remaining hostages taken by armed men at a supermarket in the early hours of Wednesday, the police and government said, ending a day-long siege. One of the captors of roughly 30 people was killed in the operation at the Exito store in Cartagena, President Abelardo De La Espriella said in a video at 1.30 a.m. from the coastal city. “I would like to inform the entire public that, through an extraordinary joint operation between the National Police and the military forces, all the hostages have been successfully rescued,” he said. “This operation was absolutely flawless ... One of the criminals was neutralized,” he added, saying that the gang had refused an opportunity to surrender. The captors, whose identity was not given, originally took about around 30 hostages in the Exito branch after a swift police response to their failed bid to hijack an armored car ferrying cash from a mall. Ten captives were earlier released on Tuesday. Before the early-hours rescue operation, Reuters images showed a crowd of heavily armed military and police outside the store in the La Castellana neighborhood of Cartagena, where the walled colonial historic district is a tourist attraction. The identities of the hostages were not known. Social media showed images of some people kneeling against the windows of the store, their hands seemingly bound. Reuters could not immediately independently verify the images. “For Grupo Exito, protecting the people’s lives and safety is our priority,” the chain said in a statement. The Rafael Nunez airport in Cartagena resumed landings after a brief suspension of about 45 minutes as the armed forces used one of its runways in connection with the incident. De La Espriella went to Cartagena after visiting the city of Villavicencio following an overnight car bombing the government blamed on a group of dissidents from the former FARC rebels who reject a 2016 peace deal. For more than 60 years, Colombia’s left-wing rebel groups have battled the government and right-wing paramilitaries turned crime gangs in a civil war fueled by the cocaine trade. Some respite came from the 2016 peace deal between the government and the FARC, but crime gangs remain hugely powerful and smaller rebel groups persist. The car blast near government offices in Villavicencio, the capital of the central department of Meta, injured 22, but there was no immediate claim of responsibility. Most injuries were minor, though one person was stable following surgery, said Mayor Alexander Baquero Sanabria. The blast hit about 500 properties, homes and businesses among them, he added. “To the narcoterrorists responsible, I warn you: you will answer for every drop of blood you have spilled and every business and property you have destroyed,” De La Espriella said at the blast site on Tuesday. “We will make you pay. This attack will not go unpunished.”

articles.title: Men charged with trespass at Prince and Princess of Wales's home
articles.summary: The charges come after police were called to reports of suspicious activity on the Sandringham estate.
articles.body:
Two men have been charged with trespass and intent to steal at the Prince and Princess of Wales's country home in Norfolk.

Police were called to Anmer Hall, on the Sandringham estate, shortly before 18:00 GMT on Monday after reports of suspicious activity.

Mirgen Doku, 34, of Courtfield Gardens, London, and Arilen Ndoci, 32, of no fixed address, have both been charged with entering a dwelling with intent to steal and trespassing on a protected site, Norfolk Police said.

The men were held in custody and are due to appear at Norwich Magistrates' Court later.

William and Catherine do not live at Anmer Hall full-time, but use the estate as a country retreat during the holidays.

The property was unoccupied at the time of the incident, police added. On Monday, Kensington Palace said it did not comment on security matters.

Dogs, drones and a helicopter were used to search the area before two men were arrested within the estate's grounds.

Anmer Hall is located on the private estate and is about two miles (3km) east from Sandringham House, one of the King's private residences.

The country retreat was gifted to the Prince and Princess of Wales from the late Queen Elizabeth II following their wedding in 2011.

articles.title: Colombian police storm supermarket to free 20 held hostage for 17 hours
articles.summary: One gunman was killed in the operation to free around 20 shoppers and employees after a 17-hour hostage ordeal.
articles.body:
Colombian security forces have freed around 20 shoppers and employees who had been held hostage for about 17 hours at a supermarket in the city of Cartagena.

Gunmen had stormed into the building at 08:00 (13:00 GMT) on Tuesday after what local media said was a failed attempt of robbing an armoured car carrying money and valuables.

They held those inside at gunpoint while trying to negotiate their getaway.

With the situation becoming ever more intense as the day progressed, Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella gave the green light for special forces and police to launch a daring operation to free the hostages, in which one gunman was killed.

Residents living near the supermarket reported hearing explosions as the security forces moved into the building.

Police later confirmed that officers had used stun grenades to overpower the hostage takers.

De la Espriella described it as "an extraordinary joint operation", which he said had been carried out "flawlessly".

He flew into the northern city to oversee the operation.

In footage released since then, he can be seen speaking into a walkie-talkie and carrying a handgun strapped to his side.

Speaking after the successful rescue of the hostages, he said that the gunmen had been given the chance to hand themselves in, which they had refused.

Earlier in the day, the men had freed 10 of their hostages, among them elderly women.

But they continued to hold around 20, even as a police helicopter hovered above and special forces erected a perimeter around the building.

Local media said that as well as demanding safe passage out of the supermarket, the gunmen also demanded nearly $2m (£1.5m) and armoured vehicles.

According to President De la Espriella, they had no political affiliations but had taken the hostages once their plan to rob an armoured car carrying money had been foiled.

"It's not that a terrorist group carried out a kidnapping - no, these are criminals who were caught off guard, had no way out, and then kidnapped a group of people," he said.

Photos taken during the rescue operation show armed soldiers inside the building while people are kneeling with their hands behind their heads.

articles.title: Iran rations electricity: How deeply are US sanctions, blockade biting?
articles.summary: Iran, a major oil producer, is facing a worsening energy crisis as winter looms.
articles.body:
Wearing a blue jacket to protect against the cold, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian pores over paperwork under a table lamp in his dimly lit office as he asks millions of Iranians to conserve electricity as an energy crisis compounds the country’s economic battering.

During a televised interview with state broadcaster IRIB at the presidential office on Tehran’s Pasteur Street, the chandeliers are switched off and curtains drawn aside to let in daylight instead.

Tehran controls one part of the world’s largest natural gasfield and has the world’s third-largest proven oil reserves. But millions of Iranians are now rationing electricity as the authorities impose rolling power cuts from Sunday, expected to last for about two hours every day.

Iran has been consistent in its refusal to bow to Washington’s demands for ending the war, which is currently at an impasse. But after months of a US naval blockade against Iranian ports – aggravated by biting sanctions and strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure – its economy is reeling, and a punishing winter looms amid an escalating energy crisis.

So, how deeply are US sanctions and the blockade biting the Iranian economy?

Iran was suffering gas shortages and power cuts before the United States and Israel jointly attacked Tehran and nuclear facilities across the country on February 28. Strikes since then have targeted other energy, military and civilian facilities .

Fatemeh Mohajerani, a government spokeswoman, warned last week that Iran’s gas shortfall could reach 430 million cubic metres a day this winter, compared with about 300 million in previous years.

National Iranian Gas Company managing director Saeed Tavakoli said this month ‌that four processing plants had been damaged during the first phase of the conflict early this year, which initially reduced capacity by 230 million cubic metres, of which about 100 million had so far been restored.

Last week, the company warned that 11 of Iran’s 31 provinces ⁠could face supply difficulties this winter, in particular Mazandaran on the Caspian Sea, and Golestan and North Khorasan along Iran’s border with Turkmenistan.

“Given the country’s fuel supply conditions, the electricity sector will be forced to impose distribution restrictions from Sunday,” Mohammad Allahdad, head of Iran’s national electricity company Tavanir, told state TV, as he announced the power cuts.

How has the war affected Iran’s power generation capacity?

Iran operates hundreds of power plants which, together, form one of the largest electricity systems in the Middle East, supplying energy to 92 million people.

Pezeshkian told ISNA news agency that “the attack on the country’s gas infrastructure has aggravated the situation and we should therefore expect difficulties this winter”.

Separately, Pezeshkian told a group of investors and producers on November 21 that Iran is facing a “silent economic war” that is “tougher than a war with missiles,” the state news agency IRNA has reported.

An Al Jazeera analysis of Iran’s power grid shows that about 86 percent of the country’s electricity is usually generated from natural gas supplies. Some gas-fired power stations switch to diesel or fuel oil when natural gas supplies are tight, especially during winter demand peaks.

Oil-fired plants provide a smaller share, generating roughly 7 percent of the nation’s electricity.

Hydropower accounts for about 5 percent of electricity. Nuclear energy contributes about 2 percent of the country’s electricity, mainly from the Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant, Iran’s only operational nuclear reactor.

Earlier in August, Iran’s Energy Minister Abbas Aliabadi told reporters that Iran’s power plants lost 4,200 megawatts of generation capacity in war-related attacks and repairs were under way.

But shortages of fuel to fire up the plants are worsening as well.

“Energy imbalance was also a serious issue in Iran even before these wars,” said Iranian economist Mohammad Reza Farzanegan, a professor at Philipps-Universitat Marburg in Germany.

“Higher energy consumption driven by subsidised prices, waste, inefficiencies, and mismanagement could not be met with a proportional increase in energy production due to a lack of investment under sanctions, and now wars,” he told Al Jazeera.

In the years before the current war, Farzanegan said he identified “fragmented governance, structural inefficiencies, and price distortions as the key drivers of chronic energy insecurity in Iran”.

Electricity shortages have also resulted in about 600,000 job losses because of the reduction of industrial production during the US-Israel war, politicians say.

Parliamentarian Nasrollah Pejmanfar told the Khaneh Mellat News Agency (ICANA) on November 21 that more than one million workers could lose their jobs if natural gas shortages continue.

How is Iran’s economy faring under US pressure?

The Trump administration claims that its Operation Economic Outcast – measures it has taken to strangle Iran’s economy by sanctioning those who do business with Iran – will force concessions from an otherwise unrelenting Tehran. Iran itself has already been the subject of sanctions by the US and other nations for decades.

On the ground, that has made the lives of millions of Iranians worse.

For the seventh Iranian month of Mehr (September 23 to October 22), Iran’s 12-month average annual inflation rate was 76.8 percent, according to the Statistical Centre of Iran. Point-to-point inflation, which compares that month with the same month of the previous year, was at 88.7 percent.

Essential goods have already been subject to triple-digit inflation for months, with food, beverages and tobacco experiencing year-on-year inflation of 113.4 percent in October, the centre said.

“The real gross domestic product of Iran is expected to experience significant negative growth in 2026 (about -7 percent) compared to 2025, which was also just below 0 percent,” added economist Farzanegan.

“This is the sharpest contraction in the Iranian economy since the end of the Iran-Iraq War, and it represents a steeper decline than earlier sanction episodes after 2012,” he told Al Jazeera.

The reasons are, he argued, “more intense sanctions combined with a physical trade embargo, war damage, and the resulting economic uncertainty and higher business risks”.

The ongoing US naval blockade on Iranian ports, which has dealt a blow to Iran’s oil revenues , Farzanegan said, is now confronting “the government with budget deficits because, despite lower revenues, government expenditures have not declined proportionally; for example, it is hard to cut large energy subsidies or increase tax revenues under such political conditions”.

What is Iran doing to address the energy crisis?

Without a relaxation of sanctions and renewed access to global investment and finance, there is little it can do, analysts say.

Last week, several Iranian officials, including Pezeshkian, said the government was working to prevent power cuts this winter. Nonetheless, the announcement that they will take place came this week.

While Pezeshkian can turn off lights at the presidential office in Tehran to send a symbolic message, two-hour power cuts scheduled from Sunday may not be enough, Farzanegan said. “If the blockade continues, these inflationary pressures will increase,” he added.

While changes in consumer behaviour are helpful for saving energy, he argued, “the real driver of that behaviour is energy cost”.

To address the energy imbalance, Farzanegan said, Iran needs to reduce the energy intensity of production, which requires the lifting of US and other sanctions, access to finance, and long-term planning. Then, an increase in energy efficiency of consumption requires investment in new production and consumption technologies alongside subsidy reforms, he added.

articles.title: 2 men charged after suspected break-in at Prince William and Kate's country home, U.K. police say
articles.summary: Two men were arrested after the incident on Monday night amid reports of "suspicious activity."
articles.body:
U.K. police have charged two men over a suspected break-in at Prince William and Kate's country home.

Two Albanian nationals, Mirgen Doku, 34, and Arilen Ndoci, 32, were charged with burglary and trespass after police were called to Anmer Hall, in Norfolk, England, on Monday night after reports of "suspicious activity" on the estate.

The family wasn't home, Norfolk police confirmed in a statement to Yahoo.

Prince William and Kate were instead thought to be at Forest Lodge, their main home near Windsor Castle, where they stay while their three children are at school in the local area.

Police said in a statement Tuesday, "Two men have been arrested on suspicion of burglary following an incident at a property on the Sandringham Estate last night (Monday 23 November). Police were called just before 6 p.m. following a report of suspicious activity at the address. Officers attended and specialist resources, including police dogs, drones and the National Police Air Service helicopter, were deployed to assist with searches in the area.

"Two men were arrested on the estate on suspicion of burglary and trespass. They remain in police custody. The property was unoccupied at the time of the incident. Inquiries remain ongoing."

Kensington Palace said it would not comment on security matters.

Anmer Hall is Kate and William's country home, located on King Charles's private Sandringham Estate. It's a vast 10-bedroom property that was given to the couple as a wedding present from Queen Elizabeth II in 2011.

They used it as their primary home during the COVID-19 pandemic and now spend Christmas and other holidays there, enjoying privacy, peace and outdoor activities.

The family spends the majority of their time at Forest Lodge, which is about 20 miles west of central London and a 15-minute drive from Prince George's new $85,000-a-year boarding school , Eton College. His younger siblings, Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis, attend Lambrook, a coeducational private school an eight-minute drive from the house.

Forest Lodge is an ideal location for the family to be based, as William and Kate can easily reach the U.K. capital, where many of their public engagements take place. Today, William met with U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham at Burnham's London home and office, 10 Downing Street.

Kate, meanwhile, is awaiting the airing of her upcoming documentary, Heal. The "deeply personal" documentary covers Kate's diagnosis, recovery and life beyond cancer. It will be broadcast in the U.S. on Nov. 30 at 8 p.m. ET/PT on NBC, on Bravo at 11:30 p.m. ET/PT, and will be available to stream on Peacock from Dec. 1.

articles.title: Could Netanyahu take Israel into another war with Iran to cling to power?
articles.summary: As Israeli opposition leader Eisenkot moves to form a government, could war with Iran derail talks and save Netanyahu?
articles.body:
Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot is seeking to form a coalition government before an escalation in the US-Israel war on Iran works to interim Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s advantage.

Eisenkot’s bloc’s 48 seats still leave him 13 short of a majority in the 120-seat Knesset needed to form a new government. But he could count on the support of the Arab parties and their 19 seats from outside the government, which could be enough to cross the line.

Netanyahu’s supporters are averse to an alliance with the Arab parties, while the ultra-Orthodox United Torah Judaism (UTJ) alliance could support either side in the coalition talks.

The Netanyahu-led Likud party’s 46 recommendations from Knesset members following UTJ’s decision not to endorse either candidate could prove decisive ahead of the initial December 6 deadline for a government to be formed.

Negotiations between Eisenkot’s Yashar (“Straight”) party and Likud remain fractious. Eisenkot has already ruled out serving in any government led by Netanyahu, but has pressed for a unity government where he would share leadership roles with another party leader.

Netanyahu argues that Israel needs a government free from what he portrays as the “taint” of Arab-party participation and can respond to what he has argued is an imminent military threat from Iran.

Some analysts argue that renewed conflict with Iran could derail negotiations, forcing the rival blocs to fall in line behind Netanyahu .

But Eisenkot has told party members he has seen no imminent threat requiring military action before a new government is sworn in. His ally, Avigdor Liberman, recently appointed to the Knesset’s Foreign Affairs and Defence Committee and therefore privy to classified intelligence, also said he had seen no justifications for new Israeli strikes.

“If we end up seeing a strike right now, then we’ll know that it’s completely motivated by politics and not security concerns,” Liberman told Israeli media.

Israel’s military chief, Lieutenant General Eyal Zamir, and researchers within Mossad, the country’s foreign intelligence service, also reportedly see no case for an immediate attack on Iran.

Although defence officials have warned Netanyahu that new attacks on Iran could trigger a wider regional conflict, Mossad chief Roman Gofman has reportedly advocated for renewed military action.

So, how pressing is the case for war, and could it really override negotiations to form government?

What have Netanyahu and his allies claimed?

In mid-November, US media reported that Netanyahu dispatched his longstanding ally Gofman to Washington, DC, to urge joint strikes on Iran, based on new intelligence Israel had reportedly uncovered indicating that Tehran was developing chemical weapons.

Several other Netanyahu appointees are also reported to support military action. On Tuesday , Netanyahu’s decades-old ally, Defence Minister Israel Katz, called for preemptive strikes against Iran before it could fully develop the chemical weapons programme he claimed was already under way.

Also reportedly backing new strikes on Iran is David Zini , head of the Shin Bet internal security agency, and two further Netanyahu appointees – National Security Council chair Shmuel Ben Ezra and Israel’s ambassador to the US, Yechiel Leiter.

US President Donald Trump appeared to echo many of Netanyahu’s claims in a November 19 interview Fox News on, although he stopped short of committing to military action before the end of the year.

“There is indication that Iran is looking at gases, looking at bio, because we’ve shut them out with the nuclear. Nuclear is much harder. And they’re looking at gas and… biological weapons, not nice, and other things,” he said, without providing evidence.

Gulf countries, which would likely be heavily affected by a renewed conflict with Iran, have reportedly urged Washington to maintain its economic pressure on Tehran rather than return to military action. According to the US news website Axios , some senior US officials are also highly sceptical of Israel’s claims, with one telling the outlet they appeared to be “driven by an agenda”.

Iran has also denied developing chemical weapons, and has compared claims that it is with the false claims that Iraq had weapons of mass destruction, used to justify the US-led invasion in 2003.

Writing on X, Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei accused those making the allegations of expecting the world to suffer “a bout of collective amnesia”, likening the situation to Dory, the forgetful fish from the 2003 animated film Finding Nemo.

Could another war derail negotiations to form a government?

Many in Israel regard Iran as the ultimate regional threat. For years, Iranian propaganda and that of its regional allies, such as Hezbollah in Lebanon, have called for the destruction of Israel as a state. There have also been repeated claims by Netanyahu, dating back to at least the 1990s, that Iran is poised to develop a nuclear weapon that could be deployed against Israel without hesitation.

“If war started, even manufactured, everyone would rally around the flag, as this is what Israelis do in crisis,” Ahron Bregman, an Israeli security analyst and senior teaching fellow at King’s College London, said.

“Netanyahu can go to war knowing that no political leader will oppose him the moment bombs started falling on Iran,” he said.

Would Netanyahu risk war rather than cede power?

Netanyahu has been frequently accused of prioritising his political survival over other pressing national issues, and some believe he could restart the war on Iran to save his career.

Alongside the multiple corruption charges for which he has been on trial since 2020 are allegations that he misled lawmakers about his administration’s failures ahead of the October 7 Hamas-led attacks on southern Israel, sparking Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, to stave off an inquiry.

There have also been widespread accusations, including from former US President Joe Biden, that Netanyahu has prolonged the genocide in Gaza for political reasons.

“I think it would be very easy for him,” Israeli political analyst Nimrod Flashenberg said.

“His own survival and what he sees as Israel’s are aligned. It’s not that he thinks of it purely in terms of attacking Iran to stay in office. He sees attacking Iran, as he always has, as necessary for Israel and a path that will also need him to stay in office.”

articles.title: In 1929, an insurance executive built a grand Greensboro mansion; after decades of decline, a $415,000 foreclosure purchase in 2016 and a dramatic restoration, the home sold for $3.85 million
articles.summary: The Julian Price House in Greensboro’s Fisher Park neighbourhood has found a buyer.
articles.body: The Julian Price House in Greensboro’s Fisher Park neighbourhood has found a buyer. The historic mansion sold for $3.85 million on 19 November, about $1.4 million below its original asking price of $5.25 million, according to Piedmont Historic Homes.The house, also known as Hillside, was built in 1929 for Julian Price, who led the Jefferson Standard Life Insurance Company for 27 years. The property takes its name from its original owner. The English Tudor-style home at 301 Fisher Park Circle was designed by Greensboro architect Charles C. Hartmann.The National Register of Historic Places nomination describes the house as a visible symbol of the financial success that followed the First World War in the city. Hillside “has the appearance of a mountain retreat, said to be the image Price wanted Hartmann to create”, the National Register nomination says. “Hartmann’s ability as a designer is vividly illustrated in his success at making a thirty-room, four-storey, 160-foot-long house resemble a picturesque assemblage of forms that merge with nature. This effect is achieved by judicious use of elements derived from the English Tudor and Gothic Revivals and the American cottage tradition.”Years of decline and renovation For years, the mansion was almost impossible to see. Overgrowth concealed much of the property. The house, which the National Register described as representing “a high level of design and craftsmanship”, was hidden behind weeds. Some neighbours who walked past had no idea a home stood behind the trees. The Julian Price House came to national attention after appearing on the reality television show Hoarders.In early 2016, the house went up for auction but attracted no bidders. That September, it sold for $415,000, according to MLS and tax records. The price was a fraction of what the property would be worth today, but the purchase gave a new owner the opportunity to bring the estate back to life. The buyer began restoration work, attracting attention from the preservation community. The house was named one of Greensboro’s top preservation projects in 2017 and was described as receiving much-needed care.In 2018, the house hosted a designer showhouse, one of several preservation highlights that year. Greensboro projects also attracted $68 million in reinvestment through the federal historic tax credit programme. Michael and Eric Fuko-Rizzo are named as the property’s owners. The couple also wanted to operate the house as a bed and breakfast. In 2019, the Greensboro Zoning Commission initially denied their permit request by a 4–3 vote.The property today includes a gardener’s cottage, a three-car garage and landscaping designed by Chip Callaway.The eight-bedroom, eight-bathroom house, spanning 6,767 square feet, first went on the market for $5.25 million.“You certainly couldn’t build a house like this again because you couldn’t find the craftsman. Everything, including each brick, was made by hand,” listing agent Kay Chesnutt of Berkshire Hathaway HomeServices Yost & Little Realty told the New York Post at the time.“This home is unique because it can be a single home again, or it’s also set up as an inn with gardens. During the pandemic, when they couldn’t host guests, Michael and Eric worked on the landscaping. They even dug a well just to water the lawn and installed lightscaping,” Chesnutt said.The listing agent also discussed the intricacy of the renovation, explaining that it was not a gut renovation but rather a restoration designed to preserve the house’s original “integrity”. “They went beyond even what Preservation Greensboro ever thought that house would be taken to.”The asking price eventually fell by $900,000 to $4.35 million while the property remained on the market.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Iranian delegation meets MEA officials to discuss multilateral ties
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: An Iranian delegation met officials from the ministry of external affairs (MEA) in New Delhi on Wednesday to discuss multilateral cooperation
articles.body: NEW DELHI: An Iranian delegation met officials from the ministry of external affairs (MEA) in New Delhi on Wednesday to discuss multilateral cooperation under the framework of the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA).According to news agency ANI, the Iranian delegation was led by Alireza Tootonchian, director general for multilateral and International economic cooperation. He met Thelma John David, MEA joint secretary (Indo-Pacific), in the national capital. Both sides exchanged views on strengthening cooperation through the regional grouping.In a post on X, the Iranian embassy in India said that Tootonchian and deputy director general Abolfazl Azizi Panah held discussions with David on multilateral cooperation under the IORA framework.The meeting comes ahead of the 25th IORA Council of Ministers meeting, scheduled to take place in New Delhi on Friday. Foreign ministers from member countries are expected to attend the gathering to discuss regional cooperation and strategic priorities in the Indian Ocean Region.India is also hosting the 29th IORA Committee of Senior Officials (CSO) meeting ahead of the ministerial gathering. The two-day meeting began on Wednesday.The council of ministers is IORA's highest decision-making body and comprises foreign ministers of member states. It provides strategic and policy direction to the association, reviews progress in regional cooperation and identifies new areas of collaboration.The committee of senior officials is the organisation's second-highest decision-making body. It comprises senior government representatives who oversee the implementation of ministerial decisions, review recommendations and coordinate IORA's work programmes.Meanwhile, the European union (EU) and IORA held their first high-level roundtable on maritime security in New Delhi on Tuesday. Representatives from several Indian Ocean countries participated in discussions on improving maritime surveillance, tackling piracy and trafficking, and protecting important shipping routes.The European union organised the event with support from its project 'Enhancing the EU's security cooperation in and with Asia and the Indo-Pacific' (ESIWA+) and in coordination with its Delegation to India.Addressing the gathering, EU ambassador to India Jean-Eric Paquet reaffirmed the bloc's commitment to expanding security and defence cooperation with regional partners. He also stressed the importance of sharing information to tackle maritime threats.Paquet said maritime security was a shared priority for the EU and IORA, adding that regional cooperation was essential to addressing maritime crime and other challenges at sea.He also highlighted the Indian ocean's importance to global trade, warning that maritime insecurity could disrupt international supply chains and affect economic growth across the region.Representatives from IORA member states and dialogue partners, including India, Australia, Sri Lanka, Kenya, Mauritius, Mozambique, Seychelles and Saudi Arabia, attended the roundtable.Participants discussed improving maritime domain awareness, strengthening policy dialogue and expanding cooperation through EU-supported initiatives such as EUCRIMARIO, EnMAR+ and ESIWA+.The discussions also covered the European Union naval force's operation ATALANTA, which works to improve maritime security in the western Indian ocean and red sea. The operation focuses on deterring piracy, protecting vulnerable vessels and monitoring illegal maritime activities.India assumed the IORA chairmanship from Sri Lanka in November 2025 for the 2025-2027 term. Its chairmanship theme is "innovation, openness, resilience and adaptability in the Indian ocean region".Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: MICHAEL RUIZ: Spivey family lawyer says no evidence points to 'stand your ground' shooting victim firing first
articles.summary: Scott Spivey's family attorney says audio evidence undercuts claims the insurance adjuster fired first in the 2023 road rage shooting in South Carolina.
articles.body: The South Carolina attorney representing the family of an insurance adjuster killed in a 2023 road rage shooting says there is "no physical evidence" that the 33-year-old Scott Spivey shot first, as his accused killers have alleged in court. "I think we have the eyewitness testimony of Frank McMurrough, who says that that did not happen," said Mark Tinsley, who represents Spivey's family in an ongoing wrongful death lawsuit against two men who were charged with murder last week. "We believe that we have audio forensic evidence that supports that that didn't happen, and I think that we'll present that at trial." Spivey died in what Tinsley has described in court documents as "a hail of gunfire" on Sept. 9, 2023, after pulling over on Camp Swamp Road, nine miles from where he first encountered defendants Charles "Weldon" Boyd, 35, and Kenneth "Bradley" Williams, 37, on Highway 9. MICHAEL RUIZ: 911 CALL REVEALS CHASE BEFORE DISPUTED 'STAND YOUR GROUND' SHOOTING, 'HE'S TRYING TO RUN' There were no criminal charges in the case for more than three years, after the two initially claimed self-defense and said Spivey had pulled a gun on them first in what had initially been deemed a "stand your ground" shooting. A civil judge later ruled that Boyd and Williams were not eligible for "stand your ground" immunity. In a 911 call that Boyd placed during the chase, he told the dispatcher that Spivey opened fire first. GOT A TIP? But Tinsley, who questioned that the case could have ever involved a "stand your ground" claim given the highway distance traveled by Boyd and Spivey's trucks, said that in addition to the witness testimony, audio evidence undercuts the idea that Spivey could have fired first. "Had the weapon been fired, [the sounds of gunshots] would have been captured," Tinsley said. "They weren't captured because it didn't happen." 'STAND YOUR GROUND' CLAIM FALTERS IN ROAD RAGE KILLING AS MEN CHARGED WITH MURDER, EX-COPS FACE ACCUSATIONS O'Bryan Martin, Williams' attorney, told Fox News Digital McMurrough has said he saw Spivey raising a firearm and that the autopsy indicates his arm had been raised when he was struck by at least one bullet. "There's no evidence he didn't fire first, either," he said. A single casing was found outside Spivey's truck, he said, with more recovered inside the cab. "When he collapsed, the slide on his gun was locked back on an empty magazine, so he had fired every round, and the pathologist testified at the immunity hearing that the location and angle of the wound mean his arm had to be raised when he was hit," he added. SECRET TAPES SINK SHOOTER'S DEFENSE IN SCOTT SPIVEY ROAD RAGE KILLING Indictments were announced last week against Boyd, Williams and two former Horry County police officials, onetime deputy chief Brandon Strickland, 43, and a 49-year-old ex-sergeant named Paul Damon Vescovi. Charges against Boyd and Williams include murder and weapons offenses. Strickland and Vescovi have been accused of official misconduct and obstruction of justice. And Boyd and Strickland, who spoke on the phone dozens of times after the shooting, face additional conspiracy charges. Strickland allegedly told Boyd he'd be taken care of and that the right people were responding to the scene, and Vescovi is accused of coaching Boyd and Williams at the scene on how to act in front of bodycams. Strickland's attorney, Bert von Herrmann, said he looked forward to presenting his client's defense in front of a judge, noting that the defense is not allowed to present evidence or witnesses to the grand jury. "However, we recognize the indictment stems from the untested state's presentation to the jury to meet the lowest standard known in criminal law." And Brad Richardson, who represents Vescovi, said he had not yet received discovery and that while the case has received attention in the news and on social media, there may be more information forthcoming. articles.title: California student Aanya Pradip creates ‘Giving Tree Produce’, a nonprofit platform connecting surplus backyard fruit with people in need
articles.summary: A student from Milpitas, California, has started a nonprofit to stop surplus backyard fruit from going to waste.
articles.body: A student from Milpitas, California, has started a nonprofit to stop surplus backyard fruit from going to waste. Aanya Pradip founded ‘Giving Tree Produce’ after noticing that many families had more fruit growing in their gardens than they could use. She teamed up with a friend to build a website during a hackathon. The platform allows residents to list their extra fruits and vegetables so others can claim them for free.According to The Milpitas Beat, the project aims to connect people with surplus produce to those who need it. It also plans to donate fruits and vegetables to local food pantries. Pradip and a team of student volunteers have soft-launched the initiative and are working to reach more residents in Milpitas.How a hackathon idea became a nonprofit to reduce food wastePradip first developed the idea at Los Altos Hacks during the hackathon she took part in. She and a friend created a website intended to reduce the amount of fruit and vegetables wasted in the community. The project grew from something she had noticed in her neighbourhood, that is trees in neighbourhood gardens and backyards were full of fruit that families could not eat.The website was designed to help residents share their surplus produce with others instead of letting it go to waste. After the hackathon, Pradip continued developing the idea and established ‘Giving Tree Produce’ as a nonprofit organisation to collect extra backyard fruits and vegetables and make them available to people who need them.‘Giving Tree Produce’ creates a marketplace for surplus fruits and vegetables‘Giving Tree Produce’ has a website and an app through which residents can offer fruit and vegetables they do not need. Donors list their surplus on the platform, where it appears on a page called Marketplace. People can then browse the listings and claim the produce they want. Pradip said collection can be arranged in different ways.A recipient may visit the donor’s home, ask one of the organisation’s volunteers to deliver the items, or arrange to meet the donor at a public location. The produce is free for everyone who claims it. This gives residents a way to share what is growing in their backyards instead of allowing usable food to go to waste.How does ‘Giving Tree Produce’ plan to get surplus food to people in needThe organisation’s work is not limited to connecting individual residents with surplus produce. ‘Giving Tree Produce’ also aims to donate collected fruits and vegetables to local food pantries. Although the produce listed on the platform is free, people can make cash donations to the nonprofit. All proceeds from those donations will go to local food pantries.The project was started against a wider backdrop of food waste in the United States. The nonprofit is focused on addressing waste within the Milpitas community. By allowing residents to share extra backyard produce, it aims to make more fresh fruits and vegetables available to people who can use them.‘Giving Tree Produce’ team hopes to reach more Milpitas residentsPradip is working on the initiative with a team of between 5 and 10 volunteers, all of whom are students at Milpitas High School. The group has soft-launched ‘Giving Tree Produce’ and was hoping to hold its official launch in September or October as of August 2026.Pradip hopes more people in Milpitas will learn about the organisation and begin using it. She said, “Tech has the ability to give life to our ideas. And that’s why I really wanted to pursue this.” The students are also using Nextdoor to spread awareness and encourage more residents to list their surplus fruits and vegetables on the platform.You use AI every day.
